note: [agent-bulk] nuecc, 5 showers, 6 segments -- the smallest event in my shard and a clean single-electron topology. Verdict shower 4000 (pdg 11, kine_charge 143.8 MeV, 2 seg, len 34.4); correction 17: it is the only pdg==11 shower in scope and the highest kine_charge object in the event, so nothing was passed over. VERTEX IS GOOD: 4000's own seed is the only segment with a point at 0.0 cm from the main vertex, and on vtx-az+065-el+20 the star sits exactly on the lower end of that segment. This is a single-prong vertex -- no hadronic recoil is reconstructed -- which is unremarkable for a quasi-elastic nuecc with a sub-threshold proton, and is not a vertex defect. NOTE THE FRAMING: event_half_span is 99.6 cm and r95 is 79.7 cm, both under the 150 cm threshold, so no vtxz-* frames were written; the vertex is judged off the ordinary vtx-* set. CORRECT, and the argument is about the non-members, not the shape (pilot section 2.3): every non-member in the event is either far outside the cone or behind the start. 30003 (pdg 2212, 4.3 MeV) is at 79.4 cm / 35.2 deg, 29002 (pdg 2212, 3.2 MeV) at 89.8 cm / 41.9 deg, 28001 (1.1 MeV) at 93.0 cm / 45.0 deg, and 31004 (1.2 MeV) at 31.4 cm / 120.1 deg, i.e. behind the shower start. There is nothing contiguous, on-axis and unclaimed anywhere to add. shw4000-acc.png makes the same point with no ambiguity at all: in the 0-40 cm by 0-15 deg window there are TWO orange squares, at (0,0) and (27.7, 2.6), and NOT A SINGLE blue circle -- nothing was rejected anywhere near this cone, so there is no just-outside-the-step case to argue about. Nothing foreign was swallowed either: the second member 47005 (14.8 cm, pass3_cone direct) sits at 27.7 cm / 2.6 deg, squarely on the axis, and cmp_div gives the whole member set as distance 0.0-27.7 cm at angle 0.0-2.6 deg. Membership triple-check per correction 16 agrees at 2 (nseg 2, owner-grouped candidates with owner==4000 are 4000 and 47005 = 2, cmp_div says 2 segment(s) plotted) -- worth stating explicitly on a 5-shower/6-segment event, where correction 16's usual trap is that nearly every segment is its own sub-20 MeV shower; here all four of those (30003, 29002, 31004, 28001, 1.1-4.3 MeV) are genuinely non-members and correctly left out. AND UNLIKE TWO OTHER EVENTS IN MY SHARD THIS ONE LOOKS LIKE AN EM SHOWER: on shw4000-az-055-el+20 the blob point cloud is diffuse and visibly WIDENS from the vertex outwards -- narrow around the first member and clearly fanned out around the second -- which is what a developing shower does and what the straight MIP-width objects I flagged on evt397401 and evt390634 did not do. So I have no PID doubt here and this verdict is a clustering verdict with nothing else attached. What correct means here is the pilot's fast-pass sense: nothing jumped out at the frames and the tables listed above, not a segment-by-segment verification. There is one small gap in the point cloud between the two members which I looked at and do not think is a defect, since 47005 is already claimed. Showers not looked at: the 4 skipped by the scope rule, which are exactly the four non-members named above. PI0: no reco group, pio_id -1, kine_div says no pi0 group in this event and no pio-*.png was written; there is no second EM object anywhere, so this is a single-electron event and no pairing is proposed. drag_check both true, probe_radius 70.7 px, probe_degenerate false.
